title: SKU review systems must preserve a distinct availability-negative disposition
requirement: Where availability is in scope for a SKU/product-based Clank's QC model, that model MUST preserve a QC disposition meaning 'this product exists and was correctly identified, but is not currently available' — distinct from a product-invalid disposition (false positive), a not-novel disposition (duplicate), and a general not-useful disposition. A Clank MUST NOT fold an availability-negative case into false-positive or not-useful. Canonical presentation SHOULD use 'Out of Stock' as the operator-facing label where that phrase accurately describes the underlying source state, but this standard does not require a literal fourth enum value named OUT_OF_STOCK — any encoding that keeps the disposition distinctly queryable (a dedicated status, or an event-type-plus-reason-code pair) satisfies it.
rationale: Returned for revision from the original Pass 1 draft (which centered the fourth enum value OUT_OF_STOCK itself) by Operator Ratification Decision 001: the operator's point was that the load-bearing invariant is ontological — availability-negative must not be misclassified as invalid/not-useful — not that a specific button label must exist. This wording protects the ontology directly, which lets oem-radar's AVAILABILITY_CHANGED + TEMPORARY_STOCK_CHANGE reason-code encoding conform naturally instead of being treated as a partial miss of a literal-string requirement.
forbidden: Recording an availability-negative item as FALSE_POSITIVE or NOT_USEFUL because there is no dedicated disposition for it
Merging availability-negative and duplicate/not-novel into one disposition for a SKU-based Clank
acceptance: The QC/decision model has a way to query 'availability-negative' as its own distinct outcome, separate from false-positive, duplicate, and not-useful

If a Clank presents a QC action set to the operator, the availability-negative option is not simply absent (it may be labeled 'Out of Stock' or handled via an availability-change event type, per the Clank's own encoding)

evidence.summary: EventReview.disposition includes OUT_OF_STOCK as a distinct value alongside USEFUL/NOT_USEFUL/DUPLICATE/FALSE_POSITIVE.
Exact same four-value vocabulary including a distinct OUT_OF_STOCK value.

Different encoding, same ontology: HIT/INTERESTING/NOISE/BUG plus a distinct AVAILABILITY_CHANGED change_type with a TEMPORARY_STOCK_CHANGE reason code — availability-negative remains distinctly queryable, just not as a fifth top-level enum value.
Operator identified the original literal-OUT_OF_STOCK framing as protecting a button label rather than the underlying ontology, and proposed this reformulation.

notes: RATIFIED 2026-08-31 by operator acceptance of decisions/0009-pass3-sku-001-decision.md (Pass 3: nine-Clank survey; the invariant holds in every availability-in-scope implementation via three encodings, including oem-radar's independent change-type-plus-reason-code design; cleanly out of scope where availability is not tracked).
